label: FIXTURE. Stand-in values for review of the job/1 shape and its pins; not an owner-approved definition. Each field names whose the real value is and where it comes from.

python_path.source: reports python-pin-probe: the resolved file the runner re-hashes

python_sha256.status: pending host probe; fixture is a macOS uv cpython 3.13.15 binary
python_sha256.source: python-pin-probe sha256 of the resolved file

python_version.status: pending host probe; decides the vendored files (typing-extensions below 3.15)

runner_id.source: the rnr_ ID the server assigns when the byotlab-1 runner registers

agent_uid.owner: Secrets owner with the host operator
agent_uid.source: the agent UIDs the runner refuses to share; the runner runs as its own dedicated user

secret_ref.source: the durable secret holding the Graph bearer, delivered to GRAPH_ACCESS_TOKEN as field value

destination.owner: Juan (the Microsoft account and app folder)
destination.source: GET /me/drive/special/approot with the real token: parentReference.driveId and id

seat_and_paths.status: deployment choice, to confirm with the host layout
seat_and_paths.source: publisher.json; the outbox is the seat's setgid 2750 export directory

publisher_uid.owner: Secrets owner with the host operator
publisher_uid.source: the non-login OS user the runner executes this job as; not in job/1 or runner-config, so proven by its own receipt

acceptance: the publisher job UID is one non-login OS user, exclusive to this pinned job definition (its job/1 digest) and to no other job, unit or service
that UID is distinct from every agent UID and from the operator's
the receipt shows the user's non-login shell, its mapping to this definition alone, and the absence of any other job, unit or service under it

the definition's env declares only GRAPH_ACCESS_TOKEN as the durable credential field value, and none of SSL_CERT_FILE, SSL_CERT_DIR, SSLKEYLOGFILE or OPENSSL_*, checked against the owner-approved digest
exec.path, exec.sha256 and the vendored file set match the host probe of the replacement lab's interpreter
output: replay writes its report and one newline to stdout and nothing to stderr in a run that completes, whatever its exit code (0, 3, 4, 5 or 6); stderr carries only argparse's usage error (exit 2) or a crash traceback (exit 1). output.max_bytes is output_max_bytes + 1, so a full report never competes with stderr for the runner's shared bound in a completed run.
